Perseverance

pur-suh-VEER-unts -- stress on the third syllable, VEER. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Perseverance is steadfastness in action or belief despite difficulty or delay.

Through failed prototypes and near-empty bank accounts, sheer perseverance carried the two inventors to their first working engine.

Worked Example

The novelist collects seventy rejection letters over six years, yet keeps revising and mailing out her manuscript until a publisher finally says yes.

Continuing steadily toward a goal despite years of setbacks is perseverance. It is not a single burst of effort but steadfastness -- holding course through discouragement that would make most people quit.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

endurance: Endurance is the capacity to bear hardship and keep functioning -- a marathoner's legs, a sailor lasting through a storm. Perseverance adds direction: it is steady effort aimed at a goal despite difficulty or delay, pushing a project forward rather than just holding up under strain.

grit: Grit is an informal word for toughness of spirit -- the nerve to keep going when things get ugly. Perseverance is the more formal term and stresses the long haul itself: continuing steadily toward a goal through months or years of setbacks and discouragement.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

surrender: the act of giving up

apathy: lack of interest, energy, or concern

Where it sits · how unshakably you hold on through hardship — persistence → perseverance → steadfastness

persistence vs. perseverance: Persistence is the broader, lighter word -- you can be persistent about anything, even a small request, while perseverance suggests a longer, harder road: steadfast effort sustained through real discouragement.

steadfastness vs. perseverance: Steadfastness can sound even more unshakable than perseverance: perseverance emphasizes pushing forward through obstacles, while steadfastness emphasizes standing absolutely firm in a commitment or belief, immovable no matter the pressure.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — per-

prefix — per-: through, thoroughly (Latin)

root — sever-

root — sever-: strict, serious (Latin severus)

suffix — -ance

suffix — -ance: state or quality of (Latin -antia)

Put it together

Put it together: Perseverance comes from Latin perseverare, built from per- ('thoroughly') and severus ('strict, serious'). To persevere is literally to be thoroughly serious about something -- so earnest about a goal that you hold to it all the way through.

Use the root in a new word: severe

Use the root in a new word: severe: The severe winter storm closed every school in the county for three days.

Root Check

Word Choice

Perseverance is the classic word for long-haul determination -- teachers, coaches, and commencement speakers reach for it when praising effort sustained over months or years. It often pairs with 'sheer,' 'dogged,' or 'quiet': 'quiet perseverance finally paid off.'
